items.note: Association name, organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery built 1891 - all in narrative 1.
Article VII quoted: paid by butterfat test not weight, and the test of the station where he delivers governs.
States the rule made the station's own testing equipment, with no cross-check, the entire basis of every patron's pay - the wrong-test-costs-money link.
Only Hobart Sill (buttermaker) named. Effie Loomis (secretary, minute book) and Wilbur Teague (bookkeeper) absent from Section A.
Selby Vose never appears in Section A; he is discussed only at B3/B4 and credit does not travel into Section A from B-G. Also dated manager from 1911 (planted error) rather than 1913.
The station-gain ledger line appears only inside C1(a), in Section C. No travel into Section A.
Ostrey Hollow, seven miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glassware borrowed from Larrow Green (Sill's outfit).
Only 'weighed, tested, separated' plus cream down / skim home. No composite sample, no percent read on the graduated neck, no fixed charge from the pipette.
Ammon & Sons, invoice of 14 April 1897, in use from 1 May 1897, and the 1898 outlier correctly hedged as Kyle's. Tarnet unnamed but the core fact is intact.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, summing to $77.93; the $77.39 variant is hedged, not adopted.
The flat 0.19-in-every-month signature is stated only at C1(b), in Section C. Nothing in the three reconstructions carries it.
Never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette and that none existed in the county. Section A does not raise the point at all.
Ansel Keddie tester from the day the station opened, twenty-nine seasons without a break, to 1925 - the service and its end. Dismissal date 30 April 1925 not given, but the item's aspect is carried.
The test book and its bench routine (date, patron, pounds, test, fat; corrections crossed and initialed) never appear in Section A.
The summary leaf's 3.80 for 1896 and 3.61 from 1898 appear only in Section C. No step-at-the-change-of-glassware statement in Section A.
The nine weeks of 1911 are named in the preamble list of turns only, with no dates, no 3.80/3.61, no question mark. No facts in Section A.
Orra is identified as Keddie's wife and as a Brant, but never as Emmet Brant's sister - at B2 the run explicitly refuses that identification. Both bolded elements required.
Section A says only that the matter 'stayed closed until 1919'. The 1919 circular's content and Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement appear only in Section B / not at all.
Death in 1934, the impounded test book and its 1959 transfer to the county historical rooms are absent.
Granddaughter, correct, resting on Falke's own dated self-correction.
Never states the chain - Ivy is Duncan Keddie's daughter and Duncan is Ansel's son. At B2 it explicitly denies that link is available.
Declines the degree entirely; 'second cousins' is called a plausible guess and rejected. The keyed answer is not given.

Abstention item A08 is about whether Emmet and Orra were full or half siblings and whether that changes the answer. The run never raises full-vs-half at all, so it earns neither half of the item. No gullibility deduction - it asserts nothing.
Gideon Vose, his father; the nephew story named as a known error and rejected with three sources.

At B3 and B4 together: Gideon wrote Article VII making a station's own test the basis of pay, and his son signed the 1919 circular accusing those same patrons - the accuser enforcing his father's rule. Section B-G scope rule applies.

Correct abstention on A01: 'none that the sources establish' is qualified on its face, and it states outright that any personal or marriage tie cannot be determined and that absence of a claim is not proof of absence.

Does not state what the record holds - two narrators asserting a cousinship from talk, one denying it flatly, no document either way. It instead claims 'none is claimed anywhere', which is wrong, and substitutes the employer-employee relation.

Key: 16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, tests read 95 percent of true, short 5 percent. The run says it could find no calibration figure and answers 5.25-5.26 percent, derived from 0.19/3.61. Different quantity, different number. Exact-match item.
True average 3.80, short 0.19 of a point. Exact.
40,000,000 x 0.0019 = 76,000 lb, with the working shown.
Answers $19,600 (planted error) and 19.4 percent, explicitly rejecting the correct $19,000 as a transcription slip. Key requires $19,000 and 20 percent / one fifth. NT-8.
Declined. Key: 200,000 x 3.42% = 6,840 lb. C2 is not an abstention item.
Declined. Key: true test 3.60, true fat 7,200 lb, owed 360 lb.
Declined. Key: 360 x $0.24 = $86.40.

deductions.reason: Asserts the loss as $19,600 (F081 planted error) at C1(d), and rejects the correct $19,000 as a rounding slip.
Asserts Selby Vose as manager from 1911 (planted error; correct is 1913) at B3 and again at B4.
